headline: Issued Mexicali Cantina Grill a 10-day suspension with 5 days served; approved several one-day licenses and a license transfer.
summary: Commissioners found that violations occurred at Marlboro Foods and Mexicali Cantina Grill, and issued Mexicali a 10-day suspension with 5 days served. They also approved one-day liquor and entertainment licenses, a common victualer license, bottle service, officer and manager changes, and a license transfer. Three items were postponed to October 22, 2026.
decisions: Approved a one-day entertainment license for The Big Dill, 633 Salisbury Street, 3-0.
Approved a one-day liquor license for Diocese of Worcester, 144 Granite Street, 3-0.
Continued the one-day liquor and entertainment license requests for Creative Hub, 2 Ionic Avenue, to October 22, 2026, 3-0.
Approved a one-day liquor license for Christopher Besaw, Commercial Street, subject to receiving a street closure permit from Public Works, 3-0.
Approved a common victualer license for Café Eidy, LLC, 643 Chandler Street, 3-0.
Approved a bottle service request for Aelux Lounge & Bar, 267 Lincoln Street, 3-0.
Approved changes of officers/directors and manager for Worcester Center for Performing Arts at 2 Southbridge Street and 2 Franklin Street, 3-0.
Approved transfer of the restaurant all alcohol license, common victualer license, and entertainment license for KAP455, 455 Park Avenue, 3-0.
Approved a change of manager for Italian American World War Veterans of the US Inc. Post 3, 14 Itam Court, 3-0.
Continued the status hearing for Hinoelia Rivera dba El Coqui Liquor, 184 Chandler Street, to October 22, 2026, 3-0.
Continued the status hearing for Carlow Clove, Inc. dba O'Connor's Restaurant & Bar, 1160 West Boylston Street, to October 22, 2026, 3-0.
Found that the violation of rules occurred at Marlboro Foods, 1442 Grafton Street, 3-0.
Found that the violation of rules occurred at Mexicali Cantina Grill, 225 Shrewsbury Street, 3-0.
Issued a 10-day suspension with 5 days served for Mexicali Cantina Grill, 225 Shrewsbury Street, 3-0.

14. Marlboro Foods, Inc, 1442 Grafton Street 
• Violation of Rules #4, #20, #21 
 
Nakula Patel and Joshi Patel appeared to answer the violation and waived their right to counsel. 
Sgt. Needham presented the following
Sgt. Needham was conducting compliance checks of Section 15 license holders when he stopped at 
the Licensed Premises and observed a store employee working at the checkout counter near the 
register. Sgt. Needham asked the employee where the business liquor license was posted and 
requested a copy of the employee’s TIPS certification. The employee stated that he did not know 
where the liquor license was posted and did not know what TIPS certification was. 
A short time later, Piyuskumar Patel arrived at the Licensed Premises to assist. Sgt. Needham 
asked Patel to provide the TIPS certificates for both himself and the employee. The certificates 
were located; however, both had expired. 
On the next business day, Sgt. Needham received scanned copies of documentation showing that 
the employees had completed the TIPS completed.  
Mr. Patel stated that it was mistake on their part and following day everyone was TIPS certified.   
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the violation did occur.

List of Exhibits: Police report dated August 14, 2026. 
 
15. Mexicali Cantina Grill, 225 Shrewsbury Street 
• Violation of Rules #7, #1 
 
Attorney Nicholas Felici along with David Bramblia and Andre Paulino appeared upon behalf of 
the violation. 
Sgt. Needham presented the following:  
On September 3, 2026, members of the Alcoholic Beverages Control Commission, Fire, Code & 
Worcester Alcohol Enforcement units were conducting compliance checks at numerous businesses 
within the city. 
At approximately 9:30 p.m., members of the unit stopped at the Licensed Premises after being 
made aware of a complaint alleging that the establishment was serving alcohol to underage 
individuals on Thursdays. 
Upon entering the Licensed Premises, the investigators observed more than 30 youthful-looking 
individuals, the majority of whom were seated at exterior tables. During their observations, the 
investigators noted minimal food on the tables and observed alcoholic beverages in the possession 
of several individuals. 
Based on their observations, the investigators determined that the individuals appeared to be 
under the age of 21 and that a reasonable person, particularly an individual responsible for the 
sale or service of alcoholic beverages, should have recognized that the individuals were underage. 
During the investigation, numerous individuals appeared nervous and attempted to leave the 
tables. A compliance check was conducted, resulting in 15 individuals being found in possession of 
alcoholic beverages who were under the age of 21.
Mr. Paulino stated that he checked all the ID cards for the individuals. He told the 
commission that he looked at the face on the ID and checked Google to see if they were from 
out of state. 
Mr. Bramblia stated that the restaurant's previous manager was fired a month before. 
Officer Harrington stated that no approved replacement was on duty on Sept 3, the night of 
the incident.  
Mr. Brambila said that the establishment takes the underage drinking seriously.  
Commissioner Cruz stated that there should have been management at the bar that night 
and the responsibility for the incident doesn't entirely fall on the staff manager.  
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the violation did occur. 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to issue a 10-day suspension with 5 days served. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Police report dated September 8, 2026.
